plain: A witness's statement made under oath and written down

webster.text: The act of laying or throwing down; as, soil is formed by the deposition of fine particles, during a flood.

more.text: The act of giving testimony under oath.
The attested written testimony of a witness; an affidavit.
The act of dethroning a king, or the degrading of a person from an office or station; a divesting of sovereignty, or of office and dignity; a depriving of clerical orders.

example.quote: There are not many instances of decisions by Juries in the admiralty or chancery, because the facts are generally proved by depositions.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 20, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
